question: What is a native mobile app?
options: An app written in the official language and SDK of one platform
An app that runs in a browser tab and needs no install on the device, such as a PWA
An app that one codebase builds for all platforms and shows inside a web view
An app that the store builds from a website without any developer work

question: What is a hybrid mobile app?
options: An app that uses only native UI widgets from the platform SDK
An app that runs on a server and streams the screen to the device as video
An app with two native codebases for one product
A web app that runs inside a native shell with a web view

question: What is a PWA?
options: A native app that the store checks with a stricter review process than for other apps
A cross-platform app that compiles to machine code for each device it supports
A web app that users can install and that can work offline through a service worker
A web page that always needs a network to show any content to the user

question: What is the main benefit of a cross-platform framework?
options: The app always runs faster than the same app written natively
The team shares most of the code between the iOS and Android versions
The app can use each new platform API on the day of its release
The app does not need a store review before each new release

question: When is a fully native app the best choice?
options: One small team must write and keep all the code in one language only
You need new platform APIs and the best platform UI feel
You want to skip the store review process for each update of the app
You want the shortest build time for all platforms taken together

question: What does the app lifecycle describe?
options: The states of an app, such as foreground, background, and terminated
The steps from a code commit to the release of the build in the store of the platform
The time between the app install and the first purchase of the user
The order in which the OS loads the native libraries at start

question: An app moves to the background. What should it do first?
options: Start a full data sync with the server at once and hold the app awake
Keep the camera and GPS on to hold the user session alive
Delete the local cache to free some memory for other apps
Save the user state, stop heavy work, and release resources

question: Why does the OS limit background work of apps?
options: To reduce the load on the servers of the app developers
To force users to open each app more often during the day
To save battery and memory of the device, because background work uses both
To stop apps from reading the files of other installed apps

question: What does offline-first mean?
options: The app shows an error screen as soon as the network connection is lost
The app loads all the server data again at each start of the app, without any cache
The app uses local data first and syncs when a network is available
The app works only when the device is in airplane mode and has no radio on

question: What is a push notification?
options: A message that the app sends to itself after a local timer ends, without any server involved
A message that a server sends to a device through the push service of the platform
A message that the user sends to the store to report a bug in the app
A message that the device sends to other devices over Bluetooth

question: Which services deliver push messages to devices?
options: APNs for iOS and FCM for Android
SMTP for iOS and SNMP for Android
APNs for Android and FCM for iOS
WebSocket for iOS and FTP for Android

question: What is a device push token?
options: A password that the user types to log in to the app on the device
A key that signs the app before the developer uploads it to the store
A code that the store gives to each paid app after the purchase
A unique ID that the push service gives to one app install on one device

question: What is a deep link?
options: A link that always opens the store page of the app on any device
A link that downloads the full app binary to the device at once
A link that hides the real URL from the user in the browser
A link that opens a specific screen inside the app

question: What is a universal link on iOS, or an app link on Android?
options: A custom scheme link that works only inside the app and nowhere else on the device or in the browser
A link that works only in the store app of the platform
An HTTPS link that opens the app if it is installed and the website if it is not
A link that asks the user to pick a browser each time

question: What is a risk of a custom URL scheme compared with an HTTPS link?
options: A custom scheme cannot carry any parameters in the link
Another app can claim the same custom scheme and receive the links
A custom scheme works only on tablets and not on phones, because of the OS rules
A custom scheme needs a paid certificate for each link

question: What is a cold start of an app?
options: A launch when the OS must create a new process for the app because none is in memory
A launch when the app process still lives in memory and only resumes
A launch right after the user switches back from the background
A launch that happens only after a reboot of the device with no network

question: Which metric shows that the app starts slowly?
options: Time to the first usable screen
The crash-free users rate of the last release
The size of the install package in the store
The number of ratings in the store each month

question: Why is it bad to block the main (UI) thread?
options: The app loses its saved login session at once
The OS rejects all network calls of the app until the block ends
The app restarts and loses all of its cache files
The UI freezes and the app does not answer to touch

question: What is a memory leak in a mobile app?
options: Memory that the OS takes back from the app when it is idle for a long time
Data that goes from the app to the server by mistake
Memory that the app does not use any more but still holds
Memory that the GPU uses to show the images on the screen

question: An app uses too much battery. Which is a common cause?
options: The use of a dark theme in the app
Frequent network calls and constant location updates
Saving small files in the local storage of the app
The use of vector icons instead of bitmap images

question: What does an OOM kill mean?
options: The user closes the app with a swipe in the task switcher
The OS ends the app because the device is out of memory
The app ends itself after it sends a crash report to the server
The store removes the app from the device after a bad review

question: What is an app store review?
options: A check of the app by Apple or Google against the store rules before release
A rating that users give to the app after they install it
A test that the developer runs on the build before each commit to the repository of the app
A scan that the mobile carrier runs on the app traffic

question: Which reason can make an app store reject an app?
options: The app has a login screen without a social sign-in option
The app uses a third-party analytics service for its events
The app has more than ten screens in the navigation
The app crashes at launch or breaks the store guidelines

question: What is a staged rollout?
options: A release to all users at the same time on all platforms
A release only to testers inside the company before the store
A release to a small percent of users first, then to more users
A release of one platform each month in turn

question: What is the difference between the version name and the build number?
options: The version name is for the store and the build number is for users of the app
Both values must always be the same number in each release of the app on both stores
The version name is for users, and the build number marks each uploaded binary
The build number is shown to users and the version name is internal to the store

question: Why do apps need a forced update feature?
options: To make users pay for each new version of the app that the team ships to the store
To block old versions that have a bug or use an old API
To make the store review of each new version faster
To remove the need for a backend in the product

question: How can an app know that it needs a forced update?
options: It compares its version with a minimum version that the backend sends
It asks the OS to list all installed apps and their versions
It checks the date of the last login of the user on the device and on the server
It counts how many crashes happened on the device today

question: Where should an app store an access token on the device?
options: In a plain text file in the documents folder of the app
In UserDefaults or SharedPreferences as a plain value
In a constant string inside the app code
In the Keychain on iOS or in Keystore-backed storage on Android

question: Why should you not hard-code an API secret in the app?
options: The store rejects any app that contains a string with a secret key
The OS deletes embedded strings when the app updates
A secret in the code stops the app from using HTTPS
Anyone can read the strings in the app binary

question: What is certificate pinning?
options: The app saves the user certificate on the home screen of the device for later use
The app trusts each certificate that the OS trusts
The app accepts only a known server certificate or public key
The app asks the user to accept each new certificate

question: What is a risk of certificate pinning?
options: The app cannot use HTTPS any more after the pin is set, until the user updates the OS
If the server certificate changes, an old app version cannot connect
The app uses more battery for each request to the server
The app cannot receive push messages from the platform

question: What does a crash report contain?
options: Data about a crash, such as the stack trace and the device model
A list of user complaints from the store about the crash
A report of the server CPU use during the crash
A video of the user screen before the crash

question: What do you need to read stack traces from a release build?
options: The symbol files, such as dSYM (iOS) or the mapping file (Android)
The password of the user account that had the crash, to open the session data
The source code of the OS version that ran on the device that had the crash
The review notes that the store gave for the build when the team submitted it

question: What is an analytics event?
options: A message that the OS sends to the app when the battery of the device is low
A change of the UI code in a new version of the app
A test run of the CI system after a commit
A record of a user action, such as a tap or a screen view

question: What must an app do before it tracks a user?
options: Hide the tracking from the privacy policy of the app
Collect the data first and ask for consent after one week
Get consent where the law or the platform rules require it
Use the advertising ID of the device without any check of the user setting

question: What does accessibility mean for a mobile app?
options: The app loads fast on slow networks and on old devices with little memory
The app is usable for people with disabilities, for example with a screen reader
The app works on old devices only, with the lowest OS version that the store allows
The app is available in all countries and in all store languages

question: A button shows only an icon. What does a screen reader need?
options: A higher color contrast between the icon and the background
A text label that describes the action
A tap sound that plays when the user presses the button
A bigger touch area around the icon on the screen

question: What touch target size do the platform guides recommend?
options: At least 44 points on iOS and 48 dp on Android
About 24 points on iOS and 28 dp on Android, for dense screens
About 12 points on iOS and 16 dp on Android
About 60 points on iOS and 64 dp on Android

question: Why should an app support dynamic text size?
options: It lets the app skip the dark mode and use one theme only for all the screens of the app
It reduces the size of the app binary in the store
It makes the images in the app load faster
Users with low vision set a larger system font and need the app to follow it

question: What is device fragmentation?
options: The split of one app into many small binaries for the store
The storage of one data file in many database tables
Many different devices, OS versions, and screen sizes that the app must support
The break of the app code into many separate modules

question: How do teams usually handle device fragmentation?
options: They test only on the newest flagship phone of each platform and ignore the rest
They ship a different app for each screen size of the devices on the market
They set a minimum OS version and test on devices chosen by usage data
They ask users to update the phone before they install the app from the store

question: What does the crash-free users rate show?
options: The percent of code that has automated tests
The percent of users who had no crash in a period
The percent of crashes that the team fixed in the period
The percent of devices that the app supports

question: What is a runtime permission?
options: A permission that the app asks from the user at the time of use, such as the camera
A permission that the store gives during the review of the app
A permission that the developer sets on the server of the app for each user account and each app version
A permission that the OS gives to each app silently at install

question: When should an app ask for a permission?
options: For all permissions at the first launch of the app
Again at each launch after the user denies it
Only through a web page of the company
When a feature needs it, with a short reason for the user

question: Which storage fits structured data for an offline app?
options: A single JSON file that the app rewrites at each change
The Keychain or Keystore, because it is built for large data sets
The payload of the push notifications that the app receives
A local database such as SQLite

question: What does optimistic UI do?
options: It hides all errors from the user to keep the screen clean and the flow smooth
It waits for the server before any change on the screen
It shows the result of an action at once, before the server confirms
It keeps the images only in memory and never on disk

question: Why is it good to keep the app size small?
options: The store blocks each app that is larger than a fixed limit of 10 MB on cellular networks
Large apps have lower install rates and use more storage and mobile data
Large apps lose their runtime permissions after each update
Large apps need a separate store account for each country

question: Why do teams run an internal beta before a store release?
options: Testers find bugs on real devices before all users get the build
The store requires a beta of 30 days for each new version
A beta build skips the review of the store for the final release
A beta build gives the app a higher rank in the store search

question: What is a silent (data) push used for?
options: To wake the app to fetch data without a visible message
To mute all other apps on the device for a short time while the app runs a task
To show a message that has no title in the notification list of the device
To send a push without a device token to all users of the app at once

question: Why should a mobile app use HTTPS for all traffic?
options: It makes the app work offline when there is no connection or a poor signal on the road
It removes the need for a user login in the app
It makes the delivery of push messages faster
It protects the data from being read or changed on the network

question: A content app needs no camera or Bluetooth, and the team knows web. Which option fits first?
options: Two native apps, because only native apps can cache content offline
A hybrid app, because a PWA cannot be installed on Android devices
A PWA, because it can update without a store release
A game engine, because lists need a renderer

question: How do cross-platform frameworks with own rendering differ from frameworks with native widgets?
options: They compile the web page into one native widget for the screen
They draw each pixel with their own engine and do not use the platform widgets
They run the UI on the server and send images to the device

question: On iOS, a timer in the app stops a short time after the user goes to the background. Why?
options: iOS deletes the timer object as soon as the screen changes
The OS suspends the app process to save resources
The timer works only while the app shows its main screen

question: Which API schedules deferrable background work that follows the OS limits?
options: A job scheduler, such as WorkManager on Android or BGTaskScheduler on iOS
A loop with a sleep call inside a background service that restarts itself after a kill
An exact alarm that fires each minute for the whole day

question: Two devices edit the same record offline. Which sync strategy is correct?
options: Block the second device from editing for ever
Let the server pick one version at random each time, and tell no user about it
Delete the record on both devices and ask the users

question: Why is last write wins by the device clock risky?
options: The clock stops when the app is in the background
Timestamps use too much storage on the device
The clock of a device can be wrong or changed by the user

question: The app retries a queued create-order request after a timeout. How do you avoid duplicate orders?
options: Retry faster so the server forgets the first request
Remove the request from the queue after the first attempt
Send a client-made idempotency key with the request

question: On Android, push messages stop after the user force-stops the app. Why?

The OS blocks messages to a force-stopped app until the user opens it again

question: When should the app send the push token to the server?
options: At each launch and when the token changes
Only once at the install of the app
Only when the user logs out of the app
Only after three failed pushes to the device

question: An iOS user denied the notification permission. What can the app do?

Reset the permission with a method call

question: A user taps a deep link but is not logged in. Which behavior is best?

question: An HTTPS link opens the browser and not the app. What is a common cause?
options: The link has a query string that is too long for the OS to pass to the app
The app has no splash screen at launch
The domain association file is missing or wrong on the server

question: What does a deferred deep link do?

Skipping tests for small changes so that the team can ship each fix much faster

question: Why must the backend support old app versions?
options: The store forces all users to update at the same time
The OS blocks old versions after one week
Users do not update at the same time, so old versions stay in use

question: When is a soft update prompt better than a forced update?

question: Is root or jailbreak detection a full protection for an app?

question: The crash-free session rate is 99.9 percent, but users report freezes. What is missing in the monitoring?

question: A custom view made of many layers is not read by the screen reader. What is the fix?

question: Why do teams track the p95 start time, not only the average?

question: A cross-platform app updates its interpreted code over the air. What is a key limit?

question: A user asks to delete the account. What do store policies require from an app that allows account creation?

question: Why should you test on real devices and not only on emulators?

question: The OS backs up app data to the cloud. How do you lower the risk for tokens?
